scope: Read official release source and PyPI 199070-byte wheel in memory; no install, no GPU, no model load, no environment edit.
decision: Root reports user approved a narrowly scoped PEFT0.5 BF16 dtype compatibility path. PEFT0.10/hub upgrade is not selected; retain this as a documented static alternative only.

comparison.result: Same standard LoRA definition with explicit r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05, bias=none and use_rslora=False: W(x)+2*B(A(dropout(x))). New DoRA must remain disabled; init_lora_weights=True.
Both versions use A Kaiming uniform with a=sqrt(5), B zero. Therefore adapter delta starts at zero, but exact seeded tensors are NOT guaranteed equal.

0.5 reconstructs a bnb Linear8bitLt subclass; 0.10 composes the existing base_layer. Constructor allocations consume RNG differently, so seed42 is not enough to claim identical A tensors or bitwise updates. This is an explicit reproducibility limitation.

Both freeze non-LoRA base parameters. 0.5 temporarily makes embedding/head originals and deep-copied active wrappers trainable, then author's explicit original_module freeze loop restores originals to frozen. 0.10 freezes originals within ModulesToSaveWrapper.update and trains active copies. With author's same freeze loop, intended trainable tensor families match: LoRA A/B plus active full embedding/head copies.

0.5 prepare_model_for_int8_training is a deprecated direct alias to prepare_model_for_kbit_training. For ordinary LLaMA bnb int8, 0.10 prepare_kbit freezes every base parameter, preserves int8, promotes nonquantized FP16/BF16 parameters to FP32, enables input grad hook and gradient checkpointing. New AQLM/Params4bit/kwargs branches are not active in this task.

0.5 non-autocast int8 LoRA forward unconditionally promotes x to FP32, conflicting with DS BF16 LoRA weights. 0.10 casts x to lora_A.weight.dtype, allowing native DS BF16 without whole-model autocast. Base weight quantization, CE and temperature need no algorithm change for this API compatibility path.

0.10 dispatch_bnb_8bit still reads target.state.memory_efficient_backward, so bnb0.45.5 needs the False state-field shim. The 0.10 wrapper does not call the bnb constructor with that keyword, so the old 0.5 constructor shim must not be applied on this path.

0.10 PEFT int8 wrapper is an nn.Module/LoraLayer, not a bnb subclass. Select actual quantized modules by isinstance(m,bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt), or wrapper.get_base_layer(), not the common class name string.

standard_int8_prepare_branch_check.method: Executed official 0.5 and 0.10 prepare-function bodies against standard-library fake model/parameter objects; this checks branch/freeze/dtype/hook policy only, not actual Torch numeric execution.

dependency_constraints.assessment: PEFT0.10 requires accelerate>=0.21 and huggingface-hub>=0.17. Transformers4.31 permits hub>=0.14.1,<1.0, so hub0.20.3 is metadata-compatible. Hub0.20.3 additionally requires fsspec>=2023.5.0 and its other transitive requirements; current installed versions must be checked before any future selection.
dependency_constraints.runtime_import_status: NOT_TESTED. No import smoke, install, GPU or DeepSpeed execution was performed for 0.10; metadata compatibility does not prove all runtime contracts.

conclusion: PEFT0.10 is a plausible method-preserving isolated dependency/API adaptation for ordinary standard LoRA plus native DeepSpeed BF16, subject to actual gradient/parameter/save-reload checks. It cannot establish historical author environment or seeded bitwise identity. Root selected the user-approved narrower 0.5 adaptation instead.
historical_author_environment: UNKNOWN. Neither this comparison nor a matching config establishes the author's PEFT/DeepSpeed versions or exact historical checkpoint/command binding.
